definition: In neural network training, a minibatch is a subset of the training dataset used to train the model for a single iteration.
details: In neural network training, a minibatch is a subset of the training dataset used to train the model for a single iteration. This allows for both efficient computation and more stable convergence in stochastic gradient descent.

explainer.lead: A minibatch is the subset of training data a neural network processes in one iteration. Chunking data this way makes training computationally efficient and convergence more stable.

tiers.eli5: Instead of studying the whole textbook in one sitting, you read a few pages, take a step, then read the next few pages.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers tune minibatch size to balance speed and memory against stability of stochastic gradient descent. A pitfall is that batch size interacts with learning rate, so changing one without the other can hurt convergence.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a minibatch is a subset of the training dataset used to train the model for a single iteration; its stated role is to permit efficient computation and more stable convergence in stochastic gradient descent. No specific formula or size bound is given.

explainer.example: Rather than computing the gradient on every training example, the model computes it on one minibatch and takes a single optimization step.
